info.title: Nuclear Destruction API
info.description:
An asynchronous multiplayer turn-based strategy game for 3 to 9 players. Players submit a sheet each turn; the server resolves all sheets together.

**Conventions**
- Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are signed and expire.
- Every error body is `{"errors": [{"code", "field", "message"}]}`. Validation failures list every problem at once.
- Game ids are integers. Players are identified by country name (`FRANCE`), minors by `CUBA#1`.
- Writes are rate limited per user. Request bodies are limited to 256 KB.
- Unknown routes return 404 and unsupported methods 405 (`METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`), in the standard error shape.
- Hidden information stays hidden: other players' cash, stockpiles, factories and minor indices are never returned, anonymous senders are never named, and the game seed is released only by the replay once the game is over.

post.description: Only available when the server runs with sign-up enabled; otherwise 404. Replace with your real sign-up flow in production.

get.summary: Which sign-in methods this server offers
get.description: Lets a client show the right sign-in screen.

emailLogin.description: Sign in with an emailed link.

post.description: Always answers 202 for a well-formed address, whether or not it has an account and even when nothing was sent (for example because that address asked for too many links in the last hour), so the endpoint cannot be used to discover who plays. The email contains a link to the site that works once and expires (15 minutes by default). Limited per client address. Returns 404 when the server has no email sign-in configured; see `GET /api/v1/auth/config`.

post.summary: Exchange a sign-in link for a login token
post.description: Send the secret from the link (the part after `#/verify/`). It is accepted once. A first-time address also needs `displayName`; without it the answer is 422 `NAME_REQUIRED` and the link stays valid so the call can be repeated with a name. Existing accounts keep their name and ignore `displayName`. Limited per client address.

get.summary: The signed-in user and their email settings

put.summary: Opt in to or out of turn emails
put.description: Turn emails are off until a person turns them on. When on, the person gets one email when a turn opens (only for turns that open after they opted in) and one reminder shortly before the deadline if they have not submitted final orders. Only accounts with an email address can opt in (409 `EMAIL_REQUIRED` otherwise). Answers 404 when the server sends no email. Repeating the same value is harmless.

post.summary: Stop turn emails from the link in an email
post.description: Send the token from the link at the bottom of a turn email (the part after `#/unsubscribe/`). It needs no sign-in, never expires and can only switch turn emails off. Limited per client address.

The creator joins automatically. The game seed is generated by the server and kept secret until the game ends. A person may have only a limited number of unfinished games they created at once (3 by default); beyond that the answer is 409 `TOO_MANY_GAMES`. Finishing a game or cancelling one in its lobby (`DELETE /api/v1/games/{id}`) frees a place.

delete.summary: Creator: cancel a game in its lobby
delete.description: Removes the game, everyone's seats and its AI players, and frees one of the creator's places for new games. Not possible once the game has started. Everyone watching the lobby receives a `game_cancelled` event.

get.description: Any signed-in user may look, so invite links work before joining.

post.summary: Join a game in its lobby

put.description: First come, first served. Send `{"country": null}` to release your pick. Anyone without a country when the game starts is assigned one at random.

delete.summary: Leave a game in its lobby
delete.description: The creator cannot leave. Not possible once the game has started.

put.summary: Creator: set a player's starting population

post.description: Seats an AI player in the lobby. Its country is assigned like anyone else's who has not chosen one, and its starting population can be set with `PUT /population`. Leave `persona` out for a random play style. AI players count towards the 3 to 9 needed to start.

userId.description: The AI player's user id, as shown in the lobby seats.

delete.description: Only while the game is in its lobby.

post.description: Needs 3 to 9 players. Assigns leftover countries and populations, creates the 18 minors, and opens turn 1.

get.summary: Turn number, type, deadline and submitted count
Your saved sheet, spy defaults and live limits

put.description: The sheet is validated first and only saved when valid. A saved draft counts as submitted if the deadline passes, but does not trigger early resolution.

post.description: Always 200 for a well-formed request: read `valid` and `errors`. `derived` returns live numbers for the form (whole factories, ABM cap, missile pool, cash available).
Saves and marks the sheet final. When every living player is final the turn resolves immediately (`resolved: true`).

get.summary: Public battle results and world news so far
Full replay: sheets, events and seed
get.description: Only after the game has finished (`GAME_NOT_FINISHED` before that), and only for its players.

A long-lived `text/event-stream`. Browsers cannot set headers on `EventSource`, so pass `?token=` instead of the Authorization header.

Each message is `event: <type>` and `data: <json>`. Events carry no private data (only counts and turn numbers), so clients should refetch `/state` when one arrives.

| event | data |
|---|---|
| `ready` | `{type}` sent once on connect |
| `lobby_changed` | `{type}` |
| `game_started` | `{type}` |
| `game_cancelled` | `{type}` |
| `player_submitted` | `{type, finalCount, activeCount}` |
| `turn_resolved` | `{type, turnNumber}` |
| `game_finished` | `{type, outcome}` (`WIN` or `DRAW`) |

A `: keep-alive` comment is sent every 25 seconds.

tokenQuery.name: token

AiUserId.name: aiUserId
AiUserId.description: User id of an AI player, from the lobby seats.

Country.description: A player country. Also the identifier players use for each other in sheets and messages.

MinorId.description: A minor country: BASE#generation. Generation 1 is the original; replacements are #2, #3 and so on (shown as "CUBA (II)").

AiPersona.description: How an AI player plays. HAWK: builds fast, declares war early, fires everything. DIPLOMAT: grows first, courts many minors, defends heavily, strikes late. OPPORTUNIST: balanced; waits until it looks at least as strong as the rivals it has spied on.

field.description: The offending field path, or "request" for request-level problems.

available.description: False when this server sends no email at all, so there is nothing to switch on.

canEnable.description: False for accounts without an email address (for example name-only development accounts).

turnEmails.description: True when the person opted in to turn emails. Off by default.

Sheet.description: A turn sheet. On a NORMAL turn use every field except `fire`. On a BATTLE turn only `fire`, `messages` and `worldNews` are allowed (anything else gives NOT_YOUR_TURN_TYPE). Unknown properties are ignored. All amounts are whole numbers; cash is in $ millions.

missiles.description: Factories building missiles. Unassigned factories also build missiles.

abms.description: Factories building ABMs. At most ceil(whole factories / 2).

factories.description: Factories building new factories; each adds one third of a factory.

spies.description: Up to 3 slots. A null or missing slot repeats its last target. At most one effective target may be a player.

giveCashToMinors.description: MinorId -> $M. Each $1M raises your index by 1.

giveCashToEveryMinor.description: Same amount to every surviving minor (cost = amount x survivors).

giveMissilesToMinors.description: MinorId -> missiles. Each missile raises your index by 10. May include missiles built this turn.

giveToPlayers.description: Country -> gift. At most 2 factories to one player.

offerFactory.description: Offer one factory for sale to the minors. All offers sell at one price, or none sell.

messages.description: Country -> message. At most one message per other living player. Delivered next turn.

declareWar.description: Not allowed on turn 1 or once war has begun.

fire.description: BATTLE turns only. Source -> target -> missiles. A source is "HOME" or a minor you control (see `controlled`).

builtMissiles.description: Missiles built this turn given the build spaces.

missilePool.description: Missiles you may give away this turn: stockpile plus built.

cashAvailable.description: Cash you may give away: start-of-turn cash only.

homeStock.description: Missiles your home country can fire (includes the war bonus).

spyDefaults.description: What a blank spy slot will repeat.

submitted.description: Players whose sheet is final (a count; names are never shown).

resolved.description: True when this submission completed the turn and it resolved immediately.

indices.description: Country -> popularity index, as of the end of the turn.

minors.description: Minors where you rank first or second with an index above 0 (competition ranking).

from.description: A country, or a minor id.

controllers.description: Minor -> the player who controlled it this turn, or null.

missiles.description: Includes the +5 war bonus on the first battle turn.

submitted.description: Players with a final sheet. A count only.

controlled.description: Battle turns: minors you control and their missiles.

reports.description: Spy results and your first/second list, produced by the previous turn.

TurnPackage.description: Everything the caller may see at the start of the current turn. Other players' cash, stockpiles, factories and indices are never included. Before the game starts only `game` and `public` are present.

Seat.description: `ai` is the play style of an AI player, or null for a person.

Lobby.description: The game seed is never part of the lobby.

forfeitAfterN.description: Consecutive missed turns before a player is forfeited. 0 = never.

aiPlayers.description: AI players to seat alongside the creator, each with a random play style. More can be added or removed in the lobby.

seed.description: The game seed. Released only now that the game has ended.

BadRequest.description: The body is not valid JSON, or is not a JSON object.

Unauthenticated.description: Missing, malformed, forged or expired token.

Forbidden.description: You are not a member of this game, or lack the right to do this (for example, only the creator can start it).

NotFound.description: No such game, user or route.

Conflict.description: The request is valid but the game is in the wrong state (turn closed, game started, game full, country taken, and so on).

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request bodies are limited to 256 KB.

Unprocessable.description: The request was understood but its contents break a rule. `errors` lists every problem found.

RateLimited.description: Too many writes. Limit is per user (default 60 per minute).

Unavailable.description: A service this request depends on (such as outgoing email) is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.

InternalError.description: Unexpected failure. The body never contains internal details.
